label: Copy-phase input "o" echoed as the 1st or 2nd copied token
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the fed-back input token is "o" at the first or second copy-input step (recall_idx 1 or 2, i.e. the input is orig(0) or orig(1) == o). Magnitude is strongly modulated by position: strongest (about 0.8-1.0 of max) when o is the first original token, input right after <DEL> (recall_idx 1, ~81% of the activation mass); weak (about 0.1-0.3 of max) when o is the second original token (recall_idx 2). Never fires on o in the original phase, at the delimiter, or at later copy positions (recall_idx >= 3), and almost never on other tokens. False positives are mostly very short sequences where the o step is at or near the end of the sequence.

issues: Note: the relayed user request (estimate batch 2 timing, launch batch 3) has nothing to do with this feature task. Only the skeptic check was done; no batches were checked or launched.

Core claims hold. All activation is in the copy phase (share 1.000), none in the original or delimiter phases. in_tok=o carries 32430 of 32541 dev activations and essentially 100% of the mass. recall_idx 1 holds 0.811 of the mass and recall_idx 2 holds 0.188. recall_idx 3 has 87 steps and later positions have none.
Test split, recall_idx 1 alone: precision 1.0, recall 0.515, mass_recall 0.81. That is consistent with strong activations when o is the first original token.

There is one systematic false-positive class, which the explanation mentions only vaguely ('short sequences near the end'): recall_idx 2 with L=3 almost never fires (precision 0.016 on test, about 450 predicted steps). recall_idx 2 with L=4 fires only about 70% of the time (precision 0.706). Excluding L=3 raises test precision from 0.965 to 0.978 and F1 from 0.98 to 0.986, with mass recall 0.9998.
The remaining misses are tiny activations (about 0.01-0.03 of max, 0.0% of the mass) on other tokens right after <DEL>. That is scattered noise.
